content.title: About
content.content: Bean sprouts are the young shoots of soy, mung bean or other legumes harvested at the earliest stage of growth. They have a crisp texture, a mild nutty flavor, and are composed mostly of water. Raw sprouts are widely used in Asian cuisine, in salads, spring rolls and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bean sprouts are rich in vitamins C and K as well as folate.
In China they have been cultivated for over 2,000 years using traditional dark‑room sprouting methods.
Raw sprouts can harbor bacteria, so they are usually rinsed thoroughly and kept refrigerated for no more than 2‑3 days.
They are a common source of plant protein in vegetarian and vegan dishes.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Bean sprouts contain very few calories, making them suitable for weight management.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: They provide a modest amount of protein useful for tissue repair.

items.title: Fiber for digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes healthy bowel function and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw sprouts can carry Salmonella and E. coli; thorough washing and refrigeration are recommended.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy, mung bean or other legumes may react to sprouts.

items.title: Not suitable for young children
items.content: The delicate texture can pose a choking hazard for children under 5.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat bean sprouts raw in salads, spring rolls, soups and smoothies. They can also be quickly stir‑fried in a wok with soy sauce, but prolonged cooking reduces vitamin C content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sprouts in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Use within 2‑3 days; discard if they develop an off‑odor or slimy texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Beans are edible legume seeds commonly used in fast‑food and restaurant dishes as a side, filling, or base for sauces. They have a mild, slightly nutty flavor and a firm yet tender texture when cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans belong to the legume family and include varieties such as kidney beans, peas, chickpeas, and soy.
In ancient cultures beans were symbols of abundance and featured in ritual meals.
Legumes can fix atmospheric nitrogen, enriching the soil.
In the US, “barbecue beans” are a staple, while Mexico is famous for “refried beans.”
Dried beans can be stored for up to a year in a cool, dry place.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Beans provide a high amount of protein, making them valuable for vegetarians and athletes.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in beans supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Beans raise blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for people with diabetes.

items.title: High in antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in beans help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking beans before cooking is recommended.

items.title: Gas production
items.content: Beans contain oligosaccharides that can cause bloating and gas in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beans can be served as a side dish, added to salads, soups, burritos, tacos, or blended into purees for sauces and dips. Soaking and cooking them first makes them softer and easier to digest.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked beans should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 3‑4 days or frozen for longer storage.

content.title: About
content.content: The diet fruit flavored drink is a zero‑calorie, non‑alcoholic beverage with a variety of fruit flavors, sweetened with artificial sweeteners. It is designed for people who watch their sugar and calorie intake but still want to enjoy a bright fruit taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink often contains fruit juice extracts, but only in very small amounts.
Sweetening is done with sucralose, aspartame or stevia, which have virtually no impact on blood glucose.
Because of its low calorie count, it is frequently included in weight‑loss and diet programs.
In some countries diet fruit drinks are classified as “low‑calorie” and can be sold without restrictions for children.
Vivid colors are usually achieved with natural food colorants such as carotenoids or anthocyanins.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: The drink is mostly water, helping to maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: A typical 250 ml serving contains fewer than 5 kcal, allowing enjoyment without extra calories.

items.title: Sugar‑free
items.content: Absence of sugar makes it safe for people with diabetes or those limiting sugar intake.

items.title: Vitamin profile
items.content: Some versions are fortified with vitamin C and vitamin B6, which can support immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Helps curb sweet cravings
items.content: Regular consumption of zero‑calorie drinks may reduce the desire for sugary foods.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some individuals may experience reactions such as headaches to aspartame or sucralose.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity in certain flavors can contribute to tooth enamel erosion if consumed frequently.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The drink may contain trace amounts of fruit allergens for sensitive people.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: A few variants contain a small amount of sodium, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve chilled, optionally over ice. It works as a refreshing snack between meals, at the gym, or in the office. Not recommended to mix with alcohol.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.
